evidence.note: Explicit baseline-first phase: ran a 20-step sanity run to confirm the script works end-to-end, then checked checkpoint size (29.63MB) against the 32MB cap and reduced layers to fit — a concrete size done-check before scaling.
Measured throughput via 50/100-step runs to estimate compute budget before committing to the long training run, showing ordered phases (validate → measure → scale) rather than one monolithic push.
Only after the tiny-run pipeline and size check did the agent launch the large training run, confirming train→quantize→save was validated first.

Grader-interface load verification, forward-contract checks, and quantized-bpb match were performed near the END, during/after full training — not locked as a gate before capacity scaling, which keeps this below the level-8 anchor.

reasoning: The agent exhibited clear ordered phases — sanity-run the pipeline, verify checkpoint fits under the size cap, measure throughput/baseline, then scale — with rough success criteria per phase, matching the level-5 anchor and exceeding it slightly with an explicit early size gate. However, the full contract/load verification was deferred to the end rather than sequenced so contract correctness was locked before capacity scaling, so it does not reach the level-8 description. This places the observed behavior at a 6.
